app.name: Tambat
app.headline: Prove that one person holds a Bitcoin Cash wallet and a Nostr key.
app.sub: Sign with both keys, publish the proof to Nostr relays, and let anyone check it without trusting this site.

how.title: How it works
how.one: Your Nostr key publishes a NIP-39 identity event that names your BCH address.
how.two: Your BCH wallet signs a message naming your npub, so neither key can claim the other alone.
how.three: Anyone fetches the event from relays and checks both signatures on their own device.

reasons.old_not_bound: The newest binding of {npub} does not claim {address}.
reasons.recovery_self: A key cannot recover from itself.

verifier.title: Verify a BCH and Nostr binding
verifier.intro: This page is a single HTML file. It checks every signature in your browser and talks only to the relays listed below, never to the Tambat server. Save it and open it from disk to check bindings without this site.
verifier.inputLabel: Signed event JSON, credential, reputation summary or selective disclosure JSON, npub or BCH address
verifier.inputHelp: Paste a kind 10011 event, an attestation credential, a reputation summary or a selective disclosure presentation to check it on this device, or enter an npub or address to fetch the newest binding from relays.
verifier.relaysHelp: One per line. Edit them freely; nothing else is contacted.
verifier.pastedNote: Checked on this device without relays. The newest-event step needs relays, so it is skipped.
verifier.none: No binding was found on these relays.
verifier.badJson: This is not valid JSON. Details: {reason}
verifier.badRelays: Each relay must start with ws:// or wss://. Check: {relay}
verifier.trust: No server is involved: the checks run here, with code from the same open source library as the app.
verifier.downloadHelp: Check bindings without this site: one HTML file that talks only to relays.

anchor.title: BCH anchor (optional)
anchor.since: Anchored on BCH since block {height} ({date}). The address committed to this Nostr key in that block.
anchor.otherEvent: The anchored event is an earlier event of this key that is no longer on the relays. The key and address pair is the same, so the anchor still counts.
anchor.none: Not anchored on BCH. Anchoring is optional; the binding above is verified without it.
anchor.unreachable: Chain servers unreachable, so the anchor could not be read. The binding above is verified without it.
anchor.help: You can record this link on BCH. Your wallet signs an ordinary transaction from {address} with one data output naming this Nostr key and event, and the change goes back to the same address. You pay a small fee, and the record is public and permanent: revoking on Nostr later does not remove it.
anchor.helpAgain: This link is already anchored. A new anchor costs another fee and does not move the earliest block.
anchor.preparing: Reading the coins of the address
anchor.preview: Outputs: one data output (0 sat) and {change} sat back to {address}. Fee: {fee} sat.
anchor.ask: Ask the wallet to sign and send
anchor.asking: Waiting for the wallet. Check the outputs and the fee in the wallet before you approve.
anchor.prompt: Anchor a Nostr identity link on BCH
anchor.sent: Sent. It counts from the block that confirms it. Transaction
anchor.noCoins: {address} has no coins to pay the fee. Anchoring needs a small amount of BCH at the bound address.
anchor.tooLittle: {address} holds too little BCH to pay the fee and keep the change.
anchor.unconfirmed: The coins at {address} are not in a block yet, and a wallet may refuse coins it has not seen confirmed. Wait for one confirmation (about 10 minutes), then try again. The wallet was not asked.
anchor.hintUnconfirmed: This anchor spends coins not yet in a block; waiting for one confirmation may help.
anchor.feeHigh: The fee would be above {max} sat, so this page will not ask the wallet.
anchor.badReply: The wallet's answer is not this anchor from this address. Nothing was recorded.
anchor.needWallet: Connect the wallet that holds the bound address over WalletConnect first.
anchor.revoked: Revoked on BCH in block {height} ({date}): this address withdrew this Nostr key. The chain record wins over relays, so this binding is not current.
anchor.conflict: The BCH chain says this address now belongs to another Nostr key, {npub}. The chain record wins over relays, so this binding is not current.
anchor.revokeHelp: You can revoke this link on BCH. Your wallet signs an ordinary transaction from {address} with one data output that withdraws this Nostr key, and the change goes back to the same address. You pay a small fee. Payment pages that read the chain then refuse this address for this key. The record is public and permanent.
anchor.revokePrompt: Revoke a Nostr identity link on BCH

receipt.title: Receipt after you pay
receipt.help: After your wallet has sent the payment, paste the transaction id. You can publish a receipt signed by your Nostr key, naming this identity and the transaction. Anyone can check it: it says "from a bound address" only when every coin in the transaction came from an address bound to your key.
receipt.txidFormat: A transaction id is 64 hex characters.
receipt.checking: Reading the relays and the BCH chain
receipt.none: No receipt for this transaction on the relays.
receipt.fromBound: From a bound address: every input of this transaction spends from an address bound to the receipt's author.
receipt.notProven: Payer not proven: the receipt is the author's claim, and the chain does not show the coins came from an address bound to that key.

chain.unreachable: Chain servers unreachable, so the transaction could not be read.

receipt.paysPayee: It pays an address bound to the identity named in the receipt.
receipt.notPayee: It pays no address bound to the identity named in the receipt.

attest.title: Attestations
attest.none: No other key has attested this binding yet.
attest.by: Verified by this key on {date}, for this exact binding event:
attest.replaced: {count} key(s) attested an earlier binding of this key. Those attestations no longer count, because the binding they checked was replaced.
attest.vcHelp: A W3C Verifiable Credential 2.0 file that carries this attestation and the binding it pins. The one-file verifier and tambat vc verify check it offline.
attest.help: An attestation is a signed NIP-32 label in which another Nostr key says it checked this binding. It names the binding event by id, so it counts only while that event is this key's current binding. It is that key's word, not a proof.
attest.unreadable: Attestations could not be read: no relay answered.

chain.agreed: Read from {agreed} of {total} BCH chain servers, all alike ({names}).
chain.unknown: The BCH chain servers did not give one answer ({detail}), so nothing from the chain is shown.

vc.ok: Credential verified on this device: the attestation signature, the binding it pins (both signatures) and every credential field match.
vc.subject: Subject
vc.current: This check is offline: it shows who attested which binding and when, not whether that binding is still the newest. Look up the subject to see that.

reason.shape: it is not a W3C VC 2.0 attestation credential (context or type).
reason.proof: it has no proof carrying the signed Nostr events.
reason.attestation_shape: the attestation inside the proof is not a Nostr event.
reason.attestation_event_id: the attestation inside the proof was changed after signing (its id does not match).
reason.attestation_signature: the attestation signature does not verify.
reason.attestation_not_attestation: the event inside the proof is not an attestation label.
reason.attestation_no_subject: the attestation does not name one subject key.
reason.attestation_no_binding: the attestation does not pin one binding event.
reason.attestation_self: the attestation vouches for its own key.
reason.binding: the binding event inside the proof does not verify.
reason.pin: the attestation pins a different binding event.
reason.issuer: the issuer is not the key that signed the attestation.
reason.field: the field {path} differs from what the signed events say.

reputation.title: Reputation summary
reputation.unreadableRelays: Could not be read: no relay answered.
reputation.unreadableChain: Could not be read: no chain server answered, or too few agreed.
reputation.receiptsUnchecked: {count} more receipt(s) found on the relays could not be checked on the chain.
reputation.receiptsUnproven: {count} more receipt(s) do not prove a payment from the author's bound address to this key.
reputation.help: Three separate checks, each counted from signed data this page verified itself. Open a line to see what it counts. They are not added into one score: an attestation, a payment and an anchor say different things. A source that could not be read says so; it is not counted as zero.
reputation.downloadHelp: A W3C Verifiable Presentation 2.0 file with every attestation counted here and the signed events behind them. Anyone can recount it offline with the one-file verifier or tambat rep verify.

repBundle.ok: Reputation summary verified on this device: {count} attestation(s) counted of {total} credential(s), recounted from the signed events inside. Every claimed count matches.
repBundle.recount: Recounted from the signed events inside: {count} attestation(s).
repBundle.anchorClaimed: Claimed: anchored since block {height}. This page reads no chain; check it with tambat rep verify --chain.
repBundle.offline: Checked offline: one count per issuer, only attestations of the named binding, never the holder's own. Whether a newer binding exists since the file was made needs the relays: look up the holder.

skip.subject: It is about another key.
skip.old_binding: It pins an older binding of the holder.

reason.shape: it is not a W3C VP 2.0 reputation summary (context, type, credentials or summary).
reason.holder: the holder is not a did:nostr key.
reason.binding: the binding it names does not verify or is not the holder's.
reason.stale_binding: a credential inside carries a newer binding of the holder than the one it names.
reason.count: the claimed {path} differs from the recount of the signed events inside.
reason.anchor: the chain does not bind the address since the claimed block.

sdProof.ok: Selective disclosure verified on this device: the holder's signature covers every field, and each revealed value matches its digest.
sdProof.addressChecked: The BCH signature in this value is for the holder's npub, so one person holds both keys.
sdProof.offline: Checked offline. Hidden fields stay salted digests; a revealed value is seen as it is. This is not a zero-knowledge proof.

reason.shape: it is not a selective disclosure presentation (context, type, holder, credential or digests).
reason.issuer: the holder, issuer, subject and signing key are not the same key ({path}).
reason.proof: the proof is not a Nostr event proof with a selective disclosure label ({path}).
reason.proof_event: the proof event was changed after signing (its id does not match).
reason.proof_signature: the proof event signature does not verify.
reason.proof_hash: the proof event signs a different credential: a digest was added, removed or changed.
reason.disclosure_malformed: {path} is not [salt, field, value] with a long enough salt and a known field.
reason.disclosure_duplicate: {path} repeats a disclosure or a field.
reason.disclosure_unknown: the digest of {path} is not in the credential: its value was changed or it comes from another credential.
reason.bch_signature: the BCH signature in {path} is not for the holder's npub.
